headline: Highest risk is medium: Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and xonsh can read/write the same filesystem, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity ingests uploaded PDFs/images and browsing context, while xonsh can read shell input and filesystem contents. If Perplexity output is copied into xonsh scripts or notebooks, attacker-controlled text can steer commands. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted into xonsh commands or notebooks without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF xonsh is used to execute text derived from Perplexity responses, instruction hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Use a manual copy/paste review step before execution.
Wrap Perplexity output in comments or quoted strings before passing to xonsh.
Disable execution of generated snippets until reviewed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the tools.
requires-engineering: enforce a parser that strips imperative text from model outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, and xonsh reads filesystem contents, source code, configuration, and environment variables. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive files to the other through copied outputs or local artifacts. The profiles do not show isolation between them, so leakage is plausible by default workflow.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, file contents can flow from xonsh into Perplexity prompts.
IF Perplexity uploads user documents that xonsh later reads from disk, sensitive data can be exposed.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files in a separate directory.
Avoid uploading secrets or configs into Perplexity.
Use redacted copies for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: isolate workspaces per agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks before uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity has vendor-hosted browsing and file analysis, while xonsh has shell, subprocess, network egress, and filesystem write access. They can both mutate the same project state if pointed at one workspace, creating write conflicts even though Perplexity itself cannot write the host filesystem directly. Uncertainty about orchestration means the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF xonsh writes to a directory that Perplexity also reads from, concurrent edits can collide.
IF Perplexity-generated instructions cause xonsh to modify files, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pause xonsh writes while Perplexity is analyzing shared files.
Use git branches or snapshots before edits.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: route Perplexity outputs through a staging area.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers and xonsh can execute shell commands or Python expressions. If xonsh treats Perplexity output as authoritative, a mistaken or hallucinated answer can cascade into incorrect file edits or commands. The pair has no documented verification gate, so the default risk is workflow-level propagation rather than direct harm.
conditions: IF xonsh executes commands generated from Perplexity without human verification, errors can cascade.
IF Perplexity citations are accepted as sufficient proof for xonsh actions, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Cross-check Perplexity claims against primary sources.
Use dry-run mode for shell actions.
requires-engineering: add an approval gate before xonsh execution.
requires-engineering: log and diff proposed versus executed actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while xonsh can expose filesystem contents, configuration, and environment variables locally. If regulated data is moved from xonsh into Perplexity, residency or retention obligations may be harder to satisfy. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so a moderate mismatch risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data from xonsh is uploaded to Perplexity, vendor-hosted processing may violate local policy.
IF retention rules differ between local xonsh artifacts and Perplexity-hosted content, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Perplexity.
Use anonymized or synthetic samples.
Document retention expectations for both tools.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency requirements.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement before uploads.
